title: As James Harden passes Kobe Bryant on NBA's 50-point game list, Donovan Mitchell says he's underappreciated - CBS Sports
description: After Harden's 51-point outburst on Friday, only Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan have more 50-point games in
body:
After Harden's 51-point outburst on Friday, only Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan have more 50-point games in NBA history
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:03 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        James Harden is in the midst of his worst scoring season since his second year in Oklahoma City 16 years ago, but the 37-year-old turned back the clock some on Friday night with a 51-point performance in a Cavaliers win over the Pacers. Harden's vintage scoring night saw him go 15-of-26 from the field and 14-of-14 from the free-throw line in typical Harden fashion for the 26th 50-point game of his career. That moves him into third all-time in NBA history for 50-point games, passing Kobe Bryant and sitting just five behind Michael Jordan. Most 50-point games in NBA historyPlayer50-point gamesWilt Chamberlain118Michael Jordan31James Harden26Kobe Bryant25At 37 years old (and 86 days), Harden is the fourth-oldest player to score 50 points in an NBA game, passing LeBron James on that list and trailing only Bryant, Jordan and Jamal Crawford, who scored 50 at 39 years old. After the game, Cavaliers' coach Kenny Atkinson offered an eyebrow-raising comment calling Harden "top-10 all-time," which drew immediate pushback from NBA fans, but Harden is an unquestioned Hall of Famer and continues to put his name among the all-time greats on NBA scoring lists. 
His co-star in Cleveland, Donovan Mitchell, lamented that Harden doesn't get the appreciation he deserves at this stage of his career, and that he expects, much like Russell Westbrook, that it won't happen until he retires. "He won't until it's over with," Mitchell said. "I hate it, but that's just the world we live in. We won't appreciate greatness. We didn't appreciate Russ in his latter years until now. It's like, 'Oh man, Russ was this and that.' It's like we forgot he averaged 28, 15 and 16 for a month. It's one of those things where we live in such a negative space. I hate it. At the end of the day, he doesn't care. And for me, seeing that, I don't care. It helps, but at the end of the day, that's just what the world is. It sucks that that's that way, but us in this locker room and guys in this league, we know who he is and we know what he's done for the game. That goes for not just him but a lot of people in this league. We don't appreciate what's in front of us on a consistent basis."
Harden has long been a divisive player among NBA fans. Some have appreciated his ruthless efficiency while others have hated the aesthetics of his mastery of the dark arts of drawing fouls. As Mitchell noted, few players have had as much influence over the game in the last decade-plus as Harden. From his massive stepback 3-pointer to his movement on drives to create contact, so much of Harden's game has made its way into the arsenal of most elite guard scorers. 
Fans will debate whether that's a good thing, but his influence is undeniable. As Mitchell said, whenever Harden calls it a career, he will get more appreciation, but there will also be heated debates over his place in NBA history as one of the most divisive stars (from a play-style perspective, at least) of his generation.

title: Harry Kane to miss 'next few months' after suffering ankle ligament tear in Bayern Munich draw - CBS Sports
description: Vincent Kompany faces a full-blown crisis with no true backup striker, putting Bayern's Bundesliga title battle w
body:
Vincent Kompany faces a full-blown crisis with no true backup striker, putting Bayern's Bundesliga title battle with Borussia Dortmund and Champions League ambitions in jeopardy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Bayern Munich's depth was already pushed to the limit, but Friday's 1-1 draw with Koln may have broken Vincent Kompany's side. Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane lasted only 20 minutes before exiting with an ankle injury, which was confirmed by sporting director Max Eberl as one that will sideline the English striker for months. Just losing Kane alone is a significant blow to the Bavarians after they didn't replace Nicolas Jackson when his loan was up, but the injuries didn't stop there as Michael Olise was also withdrawn at halftime and left the stadium on crutches."Harry Kane sustained a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during this evening's home match against 1. FC Köln. This was confirmed by an examination carried out by FC Bayern's medical department. The 33-year-old will be sidelined for the next few months," Bayern said in a statement.With this leading to a match where Bayern only put one shot on target against a side that is just above the relegation zone, it shows that this is a problem of their own creation in the transfer market. Coming into the season without a viable backup to an aging Kane would come to hurt Bayern eventually, and Kompany now needs to oversee a worst-case scenario. Luis Diaz and Ismael Saibari were already out with injuries, and when Kane went down, Thomas Bischof had to come in for him instead of a like-for-like striker. Even with Jamal Musiala's neurological issues, the players they do have aren't able to perform at their best.Already in an actual title race in the Bundesliga with Borussia Dortmund, these are the kinds of setbacks that can lead to a new German champion for the first time since Bayer Leverkusen in 2023-24, and even they had to go undefeated to accomplish that feat, while this season could be Bayern's own undoing. They've been one of the top sides in the world when healthy, but as is, this side will struggle in Champions League play, where they'll travel to face Lille. Precariously in 13th place in the Champions League league phase, Bayern won't fall out of the top 24 without Kane, but it could get close to something that they should be concerned about. Even missing out on the top eight and needing to play additional games is something that Bayern won't want to deal with, considering this injury crisis.
Being a backup to Kane is a thankless task, as it's hard to get game time and you're also compared to one of the best players in the world, but it's still a multifaceted failure for Bayern to not have one. Real Madrid were able to recruit post-prime players to back up Karim Benzema, and now Kylian Mbappe has a backup from the academy. There's no reason that a club of Bayern's stature shouldn't be able to do the same, but here we are in the same position they constantly find themselves in.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Depth issues have been what has held Bayern back from claiming a Champions League title in recent years. Kane winning the Ballon d'Or solidified that the starting XI is more than good enough to lift Europe's most coveted club trophy, and the difference between this side and the 2020 one that won the UCL is their lack of depth. 
It's a strange situation with Musiala that isn't being handled well with board members being open to selling him, and it doesn't help the overall trajectory of the club. Bayern will need to shake things up in January, but these are issues that began long before now, and to return to the top of the global game, they need to change this way of doing things.

title: Michigan goes back to Bryce Underwood: Wolverines make QB change ahead of showdown with No. 4 UCLA - CBS Sports
description: Underwood takes over for Tommy Carr, who has struggled in his run as the starter thus far
body:
Underwood takes over for Tommy Carr, who has struggled in his run as the starter thus far
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:48 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Michigan is making yet another quarterback change ahead of its clash against No. 4 UCLA (3:30 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+ Premium), as sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz that the Wolverines will start sophomore Bryce Underwood on Saturday.Underwood started all of his freshman season in 2025 and had a firm grip on that role entering the 2026 season. However, Underwood regressed under first-year coach Kyle Whittingham and his offensive staff. That led to Underwood being benched against Penn State on Oct. 17, and freshman Tommy Carr has started every game since.Oftentimes, the young Carr looked overwhelmed, and the Michigan offense didn't improve with him at the helm. The Wolverines averaged just 11.8 points in the four games that Carr started, and Underwood got more run in a blowout loss to Oregon last week.As poorly as he played before the benching — and last Saturday against the Ducks — Underwood has the pedigree and potential to give Michigan a spark. The No. 1 overall player in the 2025 signing class, per the 247Sports rankings, Underwood showed flashes of why he was such a highly touted prospect as a freshman.
In his 21 games with the Wolverines, Underwood has completed 59.1% of his passes for 3,378 yards, 16 touchdowns and 15 interceptions. The imposing sophomore also brings another element to the offense with his mobility, rushing for 617 yards and eight scores in his career. The Wolverines will need to lean on that against an elite UCLA pass defense.This quarterback change is just another indicator of the offensive woes Michigan has experienced under Whittingham. Earlier this month, the Wolverines fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck and paid him roughly $10 million in the process.
Regardless of who plays quarterback, it's hard to see this offense improving much this season, so Michigan's defense will have to answer the bell on Saturday.

schema.headline: Michigan goes back to Bryce Underwood: Wolverines make QB change ahead of showdown with No. 4 UCLA - CBS Sports

title: Mark Pope misses again by pointing to Kentucky's lack of experience after loss to Indiana - CBS Sports
description: Pope said his team is a "young team in terms of Division I experience," but here's why that claim is wrong
body:
Pope said his team is a "young team in terms of Division I experience," but here's why that claim is wrong
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:19 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Kentucky dropped to 4-2 on Friday after suffering a 90-76 loss to Indiana in Indianapolis. The Wildcats trailed by as many as 15 points in that loss, marking the 21st time in 53 games against high-major competition during Mark Pope's coaching tenure at his alma mater that his team fell into a massive deficit.When asked what needs to change to uphold the Kentucky standard, Pope went on a tangent, claiming that his team is "young in terms of Division I experience" and that guys will get "comfortable" as more games are played."They have a really high ceiling and we are not close to it right now," Pope said. "There are no magic pills. We are not chasing that. ... We knew we have a young team in terms of Division I experience, especially with our starting lineup. That's not an excuse; that's exciting because it means we can have a really high trajectory in terms of us learning and growing as guys get more comfortable with college basketball in this environment."While Kentucky isn't the most experienced team in college basketball, his claim isn't exactly accurate. The Wildcats rank No. 78 in Division I experience (1.78 average years of experience) on KenPom.com — which is above average in that metric. 
        
            
                College basketball rankings: No. 25 Indiana dominates Kentucky as impressive start for Hoosiers continues
                
                    Gary Parrish                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Kentucky's starters from last night have combined to appear in 276 college games, with freshman Ousmane N'Diaye being the most inexperienced of the group. Here is Pope's starting lineup from last night with career games played.
Ousmane N'Diaye: 6Milan Momcilovic: 108Malachi Moreno: 42Alex Wilkins: 41Zoom Diallo: 70Although Pope said it wasn't an excuse, the comments miss the mark. They also come less than a week after Pope said he hopes Kentucky fans "had fun" after nearly losing as a 34.5-point favorite against Northern Arizona at home in what would've been arguably the worst regular-season loss in program history.When John Calipari was coaching Kentucky, he would routinely field a starting lineup with a majority of freshmen in it. Kentucky has one of the most experienced players in college basketball (Momcilovic), a starting backcourt that has played over 40 games each and a center (Moreno) who spent a majority of his freshman season in the starting lineup.After losing to Indiana, Kentucky now ranks No. 66 on KenPom, the program's lowest regular-season ranking since the site began tracking data in 2010. The Wildcats are also now favored to win just one SEC game (against South Carolina), per KenPom's projections.
With games looming over the next month against Virginia, Louisville and North Carolina before SEC play begins, Kentucky will have plenty of opportunities to get back on track. However, if the first three weeks have shown anything, it's that things might get worse for Kentucky before they get better.

schema.headline: Mark Pope misses again by pointing to Kentucky's lack of experience after loss to Indiana - CBS Sports

title: MLB rumors: Freddy Peralta market picking up steam, top Japanese pitcher visits Chicago, more - CBS Sports
description: Here are the latest news and rumors in the MLB offseason on Saturday, Nov. 21
body:
Here are the latest news and rumors in the MLB offseason on Saturday, Nov. 21
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:14 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples. Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Saturday's supply just below. Freddy Peralta market picking up steam
Freddy Peralta, who'll be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is one of the strongest free-agent starting pitchers on the market not named Tarik Skubal. As such, there's healthy interest in his services. The Tampa Bay Rays, the Chicago White Sox, the San Diego Padres, the Toronto Blue Jays, and two presently unknown clubs all have significant interest in signing Peralta, the Athletic reports. Peralta, coming off three straight seasons for the Milwaukee Brewers in which he topped 30 starts and 200 strikeouts, wasn't himself with the New York Mets for the first half-plus of 2027. However, after a deadline trade to the Rays, he made some adjustments and re-established himself as a highly useful starter. The market's going to reflect his rediscovered form. 
Itoh visits ChicagoRight-hander Hiromi Itoh, who's seeking to make the leap from Japan to MLB, was recently in Chicago to visit the Cubs or the White Sox, ESPN reports. Both Windy City squads are in need of pitching help, and Itoh would certainly help them on that front. The 29-year-old Itoh ranked 26th on CBS Sports' offseason list of the top free agents in the current class. Here's part of our write-up: "A down 2026 season took some of the shine off Itoh, who won the 2025 Eiji Sawamura Award (Japan's Cy Young equivalent) after throwing 196 ⅔ innings with a 2.52 ERA. To be sure, Itoh pitched well in 2026 (3.18 ERA in 172 ⅔ innings), but he was not as consistently dominant as in the past. The 5-foot-9 right-hander is a seven-pitch pitcher with a low-90s fastball and the usual array of secondary pitches (sinker, cutter, curveball, slider, sweeper, splitter), none of which stands out as a plus offering. Itoh has thrown at least 150 innings in each of the last six seasons. He's seen as a crafty back-end starter in MLB, or perhaps even a reliever (Itoh sat 96 mph out of the bullpen in the World Baseball Classic). The Hokkaido Nippon Ham Fighters are expected to post Itoh, who turned 29 in August, this winter."The Cubs have a lot of uncertainty in the rotation, while the White Sox still need help even after adding Dustin May this offseason. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mets getting calls on Vientos
The New York Mets retained the services of first baseman Mark Vientos leading up to the recent non-tender deadline despite his pattern of decline over the last two seasons. Now, Vientos could be on the move. The soon-to-be 27-year-old has been the subject of trade inquiries, The Athletic reports. While Vientos is coming off a highly disappointing 2026 season, he still has power potential and in his semi-recent past a 2024 campaign in which he hit 27 home runs in 111 games. All of that makes Vientos a fairly compelling change-of-scenery possibility, and the Mets may seek to make that happen this winter.

title: NWSL Championship 2026 picks: Will the Washington Spirit or the Kansas City Current reach the top? - CBS Sports
description: Our experts unanimously back one of the finalists to take home the title on Saturday night
body:
Our experts unanimously back one of the finalists to take home the title on Saturday night
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:46 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For the third straight time, the Washington Spirit are playing for the NWSL Championship. The No. 3 Spirit host the No. 4 Kansas City Current at Audi Field on Saturday for the biggest prize in domestic women's soccer. Kickoff is at 8 p.m. ET, and you can see it all on CBS and Paramount+. The Washington Spirit won it all in 2021 but came up just short in each of the last two finals. This may be the day that Trinity Rodman gets her second crown.The Kansas City Current bring plenty to the final and may just be the favorites. They're back in the big game for the first time since 2022 after ending NJ/NY Gotham FC's title defense in the semis. Croix Bethune, who used to play for the Spirit, curled in a free-kick stunner, and Haley Hopkins won it in the 89th minute.So who lifts the trophy? Our experts make their picks below.NWSL Championship Picks
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Pardeep Cattry
                            
            
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Sandra Herrera
                            
            
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Chuck Booth
                            
            ChampionsWashington SpiritWashington SpiritWashington SpiritFinal score2-12-12-1MVPTrinity RodmanClara Luvanga Trinity RodmanBiggest keyStar-studded attack: This year's finalists did not have the most straightforward journeys to the NWSL Championship, but the good news for each of them is that there will be few excuses when they finally take to the pitch on Saturday. Trinity Rodman is about to cap off a career-best campaign after an injury-riddled 2025 season and will be joined by the impactful Sofia Cantore and midseason arrival Clara Luvanga, putting the Washington Spirit in as good a position as any to come out with a win that has eluded them over the last two seasons. The Current, though, are in the same boat --  they have struggled without their all-star trio, but each of Croix Bethune, Temwa Chawinga and Michelle Cooper will be available on Saturday and equally capable of turning the game in their favor.
Midfield battles: There's going to be a real display of veteran prowess and eager energy. Both teams have experienced players and rising stars, and it'll be a combo of chess and tug of war during the NWSL Championship. Washington Spirit's Andi Sullivan anchors most things in the middle, with Leicy Santos linking play and Melissa Bethi's recent rise in form. Even with all the changes from injuries to departures and returns from maternity leave, the Spirit are gelling at a good time in a crucial part of the pitch. They'll battle against Kansas City's Lo'eau LaBonta and Vanessa DiBernardo, two of the best in the league with longevity and finesse. Ball knowers understand that they're two players who can control a game, close and create lanes, or serve up goals and assists. Add attacking mid Croix Bethune into the mix, and Kansas City have plenty of ways to win the middle of the park.  -- Sandra HerreraBalance: At their best, the Washington Spirit are a side who can win a game in multiple ways, and while there's plenty of star power on both sides, balance is where they win out. It's a fascinating match for both sides and one where the margins will be thin but being able to have a strong attack led by Trinity Rodman along with a buildup that Andi Sullivan keeps control of. If the Spirit can control the pace, it will be a long day for Kansas City but Croix Bethune will have ideas of her own as well.  -- Chuck BoothChampionsWashington Spirit: The Spirit have tossed around the phrase that the third time's the charm after two empty-handed trips to the NWSL Championship and this year, it's hard not to buy the argument. Rodman is happy and healthy but she is just one part of a team that has been smartly assembled over the years and seems as cohesive as ever. -- Pardeep Cattry
Washington Spirit: Truthfully, the pressure is on the Washington Spirit headed into this one, and that typically doesn't play out the best for teams who are the higher seed or considered favorites on paper. Kansas City will be a more than worthy opponent, but the Spirit's third time in the final comes with a long home build-up through and back to Audi Field, and any mental component needed will come with a boost from the crowd environment. -- Sandra HerreraWashington Spirit: Sure, this is a "neutral" venue, but being a home team in a final match will carry the Spirit at Rowdy Audi. Considering that this is the third consecutive final, fans snatched up tickets as soon as they could, assuming that the home side would be here. While all the pressure is on the Spirit and rightfully so, the team has also embraced that, and once the first goal goes in the net, this is going to turn into a party.  -- Chuck BoothMVPTrinity Rodman: Is this an obvious choice? Yes, yes it is, but to be fair, Rodman has earned the right to be the easy pick. She has always been key to the Spirit's success but hit a new level this season, to the point that she had a very valid MVP case even if her ex-teammate Ashley Sanchez took it home instead after a record-breaking season with the North Carolina Courage. Rodman's ability to create and score chances means she's very likely to have a say on Saturday, one that could very well end the Spirit's five-year wait for another championship. -- Pardeep Cattry
Clara Luvanga: The last few NWSL Championship MVPs have gone to the lone goal scorer. Barbra Banda won it in 2024 for her game-winning goal, and Rose Lavelle earned it for her single title goal in 2025. If these two teams match up on the pitch as evenly as they do on paper, then it could come down to a single moment again, and Luvanga has shown she's better positioned for it with her current form. Her four goals and three assists through seven games make her an efficient threat on goal, and could finally be the difference maker for the group in their third final. -- Sandra HerreraTrinity Rodman: To win finals, you need your best players to be at their best. All eyes have been on Trinity Rodman this season after she became the highest-paid player in NWSL history, and she has delivered. Considering that the next development in her career is to become a player for the biggest moments, and capping off the final by scoring will be just the way to do it. -- Chuck Booth

title: College basketball rankings: No. 25 Indiana dominates Kentucky as impressive start for Hoosiers continues - CBS Sports
description: The Hoosiers remain at No. 25 after cruising past rival Kentucky and putting Mark Pope's squad in serious early-s
body:
The Hoosiers remain at No. 25 after cruising past rival Kentucky and putting Mark Pope's squad in serious early-season trouble
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:16 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Indiana started 7-0 last season and still missed the NCAA Tournament with an 18-14 record. So I understand those with a pump-the-brakes attitude.But doesn't this start feel different?It certainly looks different. And in terms of the quality of the wins, it's undeniably different following Friday's 90-76 blowout of Kentucky inside Lucas Oil Stadium that pushed the Hoosiers to 6-0 with three victories over schools ranked inside the top 80 at KenPom. Last season's 7-0 start at Indiana featured zero wins over schools that finished ranked inside the top 80 at KenPom -- and five of those first seven wins were over teams that finished ranked 240th-or-worse.Again, this season's 6-0 start features three wins over schools ranked inside the top 80 -- specifically Arkansas (No. 38), Kentucky (No. 63) and Syracuse (No. 78). For what it's worth, Arkansas and Kentucky -- John Calipari's current school and his old school -- were both in the preseason AP Top 25 poll, meaning the only schools with multiple wins over teams in the preseason Top 25 are Houston, Memphis and Indiana.Will this be the season the Hoosiers get back to the Sweet 16 for the first time since Tom Crean guided them there in 2016? As always, we'll see. But there's no denying they're off to a nice start, one that has more substance to it than the start IU put together last season.Indiana is No. 25 in Saturday morning's updated CBS Sports Top 25 And 1 daily college basketball rankings, where Houston remains No. 1 for the third straight morning. As for Kentucky, I mean, yuck.
As I've noted many times on the Eye On College Basketball Podcast, nobody needed an encouraging start to the season more than third-year UK coach Mark Pope.So far, it's going terribly.The Wildcats are 4-2 with no good wins, a 20-point loss to Kansas and a 14-point loss to Indiana. They're down to 63rd at KenPom and 64th at BartTorvik. Even worse, when you remove the preseason data from the rankings at Torvik, Kentucky drops all the way down to 115th.And did you see the updated projections at KenPom?
It now has the Wildcats entering the SEC Tournament with a 16-16 record, including a 6-12 mark in the SEC. Needless to say, barring something surprising, that would result in a coaching change at UK, a place that has spent big money on rosters each of the past two seasons but is -- to date -- getting a poor return on its investment. title: JuJu Watkins noncommittal on entering 2027 WNBA Draft after season-high 36 points over Baylor: 'I don't know' - CBS Sports
description: The Tempo have the No. 1 pick in April's lottery, but for now, Watkins is staying focused on USC
body:
The Tempo have the No. 1 pick in April's lottery, but for now, Watkins is staying focused on USC
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:38 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        INGLEWOOD, CA -- Although JuJu Watkins is the top prospect for the 2027 WNBA Draft, the USC star told reporters that she has not yet made a decision on whether she will declare for the draft or stay with the Trojans another year. "As far as the next thing, honestly, all my attention is here," Watkins responded on Friday night when asked about what is factoring into her decision. "I really can't say what I'm doing because I don't know. I'm just locked in on everything we have going on here, honestly."
The Tempo secured the No. 1 overall pick during last week's WNBA Draft Lottery, meaning Toronto would likely end up being Watkins' next destination if she does decide to declare. However, nothing is guaranteed because Notre Dame star Hannah Hidalgo already made it clear she does plan on declaring and is ready to compete for that No. 1 spot. A quick side note on that: Mark your calendars because Watkins and Hidalgo will be facing off on Dec. 19 at the Players Era Showcase in Las Vegas.
Watkins missed 588 days after tearing her ACL during the 2025 NCAA Tournament and, understandably so, she wants to feel things out since she has only played five games in her return."I've been gone for so long that honestly I'm just trying to learn as much as possible and translate it into the next game that we have," she said when asked if there's any specific part of her game she is focused on.Despite the long break, Watkins is off to a pretty solid start. She is averaging 24.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 3.3 steals and 1.3 blocks per game. 
Watkins shines against BaylorUSC picked up a 78-69 victory against Baylor at Intuit Dome on Friday night, and although the Bears threw the first punch, Baylor coach Nicki Collen highlighted one key reason her team fell short: "JuJu got us."Watkins registered a season-high 36 points on 48.1% shooting and completed the double-double with 11 rebounds. She also added four assists, six steals and one block. Perhaps the most impressive part is that she played 39 minutes while recovering from a cold. The USC star had hardly any voice left after the game, and yet she still managed to turn heads while playing on the Clippers' court.
Collen recalled coaching against Watkins during the 2024 Sweet Sixteen in Portland. Watkins scored 30 points in that 74-70 USC win, but the Baylor coach pointed out that she was not as efficient in that one, as she went 8 of 28 from the field. Yet, the biggest difference Collen noticed between that game and the one on Saturday was how much Watkins has grown on defense.
"I think there is a totally different effort at the defensive end," Collen said. "I felt like when we played against her as a freshman, we wanted to put her into actions. Any actions we could put her in, we wanted her in. We wanted to back cut her, we wanted to move her around, we wanted to get her in screens. "And then she goes and has six steals today, so I think she's made a huge jump in that area. Which, when you think about her size, quickness, she has such a burst. So I think she has a chance to be a really elite two-way player at the next level."Whether or not Watkins decides to go pro next year, at least the Trojans get to benefit from her return this season. USC is currently No. 4 in the nation with a 4-1 record. The lone loss was a respectable fight against No. 1 South Carolina earlier this the week. Watkins and the rest of the Trojans will be back on the court on Monday, Nov. 23, when they host Northern Arizona at Galen Center.

title: How to watch 49ers vs. Vikings in Mexico City: TV, streaming, betting odds for 'Sunday Night Football' clash - CBS Sports
description: The NFC-leading 49ers face the Vikings in a Mexico City duel at Estadio Azteca
body:
The NFC-leading 49ers face the Vikings in a Mexico City duel at Estadio Azteca
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:47 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The biggest game of Week 11 -- and arguably the biggest game of the season so far -- goes down on "Sunday Night Football," when the San Francisco 49ers face the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.The 49ers (8-1) lead the NFC, while the Vikings (7-2) are tied for the conference's second-best record. Not only that, but it's a classic matchup of unstoppable force meeting immovable object.Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense are coming off a 46-point performance in a win over the Cowboys and have been cooking all season. San Francisco leads the NFL in yards per game and yards per play and is third in offensive points scored per game. Purdy is having arguably his best season, and he leads the league with 9.0 yards per attempt.But Brian Flores' defense could provide the toughest test yet. The Vikings' defense is second in yards allowed per game and yards allowed per play. Blitzing at the league's highest rate by far, Minnesota leads the NFL in pressure rate and sack rate by a wide margin.

        
            
                With Kyle Shanahan and Brian Flores, Vikings-49ers will be a matchup for the modern NFL
                
                    JP Acosta                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The duel between Flores and Kyle Shanahan is the clear headliner here, but it's far from the only one. Looking at the Vikings' offense against the 49ers' defense, Kirk Cousins makes his second start for Minnesota after returning to the team at the trade deadline. Cousins threw a pair of touchdown passes in his first game back, a 30-10 Week 10 romp over the Packers, and he has looked as good as ever since his 2023 Achilles tear ended his first stint in Minnesota.The San Francisco defense, meanwhile, doesn't garner the same headlines, but it ranks fourth in yards per play. Cousins and Justin Jefferson trying to crack one of the league's stiffest defenses will be key to this monster showdown, too.It's also worth noting this game is being played at significant altitude. Here's how the 49ers and the Vikings are trying to adapt. 
How to watch 49ers vs. VikingsDate: Sunday, Oct. 25 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: Estadio Azteca (Mexico City)TV: NBC | Stream: fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: 49ers -3 via DraftKings SportsbookWhat to knowHow does Brock Purdy fare against pressure? Purdy has been outstanding against pressure this year, leading the NFL in completion percentage (58%) and ranking third in yards per attempt (8.5) in those situations. He has also thrown just one interception when pressured. But Flores' pressures aren't like normal pressures. The Vikings blitz on 72% of opponent dropbacks, by far the highest rate in the league, and when they get pressure, opponents average just 2.2 yards per play, the second-lowest rate in the league. In two games against Flores' defense, Purdy has thrown just two interceptions (compared to three picks) and has been sacked on nearly 10% of his dropbacks. Purdy is better than his past self, but the Vikings' defense is, too.Will Mike Evans play? The 49ers have been without Evans ever since he left near halftime in Week 6 against the Commanders. The star wide receiver has been dealing with Achilles issues all season, but he's officially questionable for Sunday night, and Shanahan said, "he's going in the right direction."https://x.com/RapSheet/status/2123864564974460973ESPN reported that Evans has "a real chance to go." If Evans does indeed play, it'd be a massive boost for San Francisco. In Evans' last full game, he had seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Seahawks, and his ability to win contested catches would be huge for Purdy against such an aggressive defense.
What can Kirk Cousins produce in his second game? Cousins completely changed the Vikings' offense -- both in terms of structure and results -- in Week 10. The Vikings' 30 points were their most since Week 1. Cousins converted several third-and-longs and gave Jefferson his healthiest workload of the season: nine catches on 13 targets. The 49ers do an excellent job limiting explosive plays, but Jefferson is an explosive play waiting to happen, and now he has a quarterback who can feed him.PredictionThis is a true best-vs.-best matchup, but perhaps the least talked-about unit will play the biggest role. The 49ers' defense is truly elite, and linebacker Fred Warner is making a legitimate Defensive Player of the Year case at a position that rarely wins the award. Purdy will make enough plays, even if the Vikings limit the San Francisco attack overall, and the 49ers emerge with a close win. Pick: 49ers 20, Vikings 17

title: Dabo Swinney fires off at critics 'inside and outside of Clemson' following gutsy win over Duke - CBS Sports
description: Swinney took had a strong response for those doubting him in the wake of the Georgia Tech loss last week
body:
Swinney took had a strong response for those doubting him in the wake of the Georgia Tech loss last week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:44 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the wake of Clemson's ugly 20-6 loss to Georgia Tech last week, Dabo Swinney faced another wave of well-earned criticism from all angles. Friday night's gutsy 20-10 win over Duke gave Swinney a chance to fire back, and he took it."So many people have quit on our team, inside and outside of Clemson, honestly," Swinney said. "There ain't no quit in our staff. There ain't no quit in our staff. It's hard to win. That was a ranked team, and I think we were a 13-point underdog, and we found a way to win the game."Down to third-string quarterback Trent Pearman, the Tigers adapted as well as they could on offense. Pearman threw the ball 27 times for just 164 yards, but he and receiver-turned-quarterback Chris Denson combined to run the ball 22 times for 122 yards and two touchdowns.
Defensively, Clemson turned in one of its best performances of the season. Blue Devils quarterback Walker Eget averaged just 3.8 yards per attempt through the air while throwing an interception. Star running back Nate Sheppard broke loose for a 55-yard touchdown, but he totaled just 61 yards on his other 18 carries.
The Tigers showed serious resilience in bouncing back from that loss to the Yellow Jackets, and Swinney heralded his players for their fight."They're not quitters," Swinney said. "They're fighters."In his postgame press conference, Swinney was clearly galvanized by the win. He tripled down on his way of doing things and took shots at everyone, including what might've been some thinly-veiled jabs at his own athletic department.Dabo vs. the worldAs Clemson players celebrated on the Wallace Wade Stadium field, they encountered a fan holding up a "Support Swinney" sign. The Tigers borrowed the sign and echoed the same sentiment to anyone within earshot.
"I saw a fan with a sign, and I appreciate that," Swinney said. "I've been here for 24 years; I've given my life to this place. I've tried to represent Clemson with class and integrity.""I appreciate that there's at least one fan that went to Wal-Mart, got some poster board and wrote, 'I support Coach Swinney,'" Swinney added later. "I appreciate that. I'm glad to know there's one out there."Those answers encompassed the tone of Swinney's entire press conference. The constant criticism of Swinney and his antiquated ways of doing business in the modern landscape had clearly rubbed him the wrong way, and Friday night was his chance to unload.
"Y'all like to ask me all these antagonistic stupid questions at a Tuesday press conference so we can have all this clickbait and all this bullcrap," Swinney said. "Everybody can write all these crazy articles and stupid stuff and trash me. It hurts me because I've done nothing but do my best here for 24 years."Following last week's loss to Georgia Tech, Clemson athletic director Graham Neff admitted that the athletic department has heard from disillusioned fans about the entire Clemson football experience — from the on-field product to the game-day experience. Neff also acknowledged the need to adapt in the NIL and transfer portal world.Swinney has been hesitant to embrace those new realities at Clemson, and it doesn't sound like that will change anytime soon. The longtime Tigers coach said he intends to remain true to himself.
"I know people want me to be different, but I'm gonna be me," Swinney said. "If that's not good enough, that's not good enough. I'm like Chick-fil-A. I'm closed on Sunday. Everybody else wants me to be open on Sunday. Well, they can get somebody else to do it. I'm gonna be me."If no one else — fans, media or his own athletic department — will stand up for Swinney in the face of loud criticism, he'll certainly stand up for himself."Nobody else defends me," Swinney said. "Nobody else stands up for Coach Swinney, except them freakin' players that know."

body:
Tony Pollard faces his former team, Justin Jefferson reunites with Kirk Cousins on an international stage and Josh Downs makes his Chiefs home debut
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:41 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        This week in the NFL, Fernando Mendoza makes his second career start against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense coming off a bye, the Jacksonville Jaguars will get tested by J.J. McCarthy and the New York Giants, while the Minnesota Vikings take on the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City in what could be the "Sunday Night Football" matchup of the year. Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a veteran tight end. Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. TE Mark Andrews (+310)Mark Andrews was Jacoby Brissett's go-to target in his first start for the Baltimore Ravens. The tight end caught all eight of his targets for 82 yards against the Los Angeles Chargers. Those eight targets marked a season-high for Andrews, as did his 82 yards -- which led the team. This Carolina Panthers defense the Ravens are up against on Sunday allows 26.2 points per game, which is tied for 25th in the NFL. Carolina actually allows 38.5 points per game at home. I can see Andrews finding pay dirt during a red-zone trip.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. WR Josh Downs (+205)It was fun to see the Kansas City Chiefs passing attack take off against the Atlanta Falcons last week. Patrick Mahomes threw for 348 yards and a whopping five touchdowns. We can't credit trade-deadline addition Josh Downs alone for this resurgence, but the former Colt did catch four passes for 53 yards and a touchdown.
This week, the Chiefs host the 3-7 Arizona Cardinals -- who are 16.5-point underdogs! The Cardinals are tied in having allowed the most passing touchdowns this season with 22. I'll take Downs to find the end zone in his first home game as a Chief. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. RB Tony Pollard (-130)Again, I hate paying a -130 price straight up, but this could be a parlay leg. Parlay it with the Over in this game! The Tennessee Titans and Dallas Cowboys statistically have the two worst defenses in the NFL.Tony Pollard has rushed for 279 yards with 112 receiving yards and scored six total touchdowns over the past three games. He's been great, and now faces off against his former team, who allows more rushing yards per game (154.1) than any other club. Spotrac mentioned that Pollard is one rushing touchdown away from a $200K bonus. The former Cowboy scores on Sunday. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. RB Omarion Hampton (+120)How about Chargers running back Omarion Hampton last week? He rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown in L.A.'s first win of the season in Baltimore. Good things happened when he got the ball, which is something I think offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel realized. This week, the Chargers host the flailing New York Jets, who allow 135.3 rushing yards per game. That ranks third-worst in the NFL.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. WR Justin Jefferson (+115)Justin Jefferson is surely excited that Kirk Cousins is back. He caught nine balls on 13 targets for 74 yards in the Week 10 win over the Green Bay Packers. Those nine receptions marked a season-high, and the 13 targets were the most he's seen in a game in two years.The 49ers will surely be a tough test for this new-look Vikings offense, but Jefferson remains Cousins' go-to weapon. I'll take him to score and break out the "Griddy" in Mexico.
